svg.text: On the wire: IDLE sequence, packet, and one level of preemption
IDLE (6 characters, never scrambled, LFSR does not advance)
b0 scr b1 lock b2 inv
CRC8 covers polarity, seed, flags (skip may be added or dropped by an elastic buffer)
CRC8 covers polarity, seed, flags (skip may be added or dropped by an elastic buffer)
Sent at least every 5000 characters (4470 when locked, 32 while either end is unlocked).
Receiver: polarity from the character after the comma, then loads the seed into its
descrambler in the CRC character's cycle so the very next character decodes.
Packet (SOP + 3 + payload + 2 + EOP, at most 262 characters)
CRC16 (CCITT 0x1021, seed 0xFFFF) covers the payload; residue 0x0000 good, 0x1D0F sender aborted
CRC16 (CCITT 0x1021, seed 0xFFFF) covers the payload; residue 0x0000 good, 0x1D0F sender aborted
Everything between SOP and EOP is scrambled
(xor with the LFSR, CRCs computed on plaintext).
Preemption: channel 1 interrupts a channel 2 packet (one level, once per packet)
preempting packet: K27.7 is its SOP, the first EOP closes it
preempting packet: K27.7 is its SOP, the first EOP closes it
outer packet resumes and the second EOP closes it
outer packet resumes and the second EOP closes it
Receiver keeps two parse contexts, each with its own CRC16 and a three character delay line, so the
outer packet is frozen while the preempting one is delivered and then picks up where it stopped. On the
user side this shows as a gap in valid on channel 2 while channel 1's beats come out. Only one channel
(PREEMPT_CHANNEL) may preempt, only into a payload, and only once per outer packet; that bound keeps the
worst case comma-to-comma gap at interval + 2 x 262 + 2 and is why the locked interval defaults to 4470.
